info.title: CityTurfer API
info.description:
The CityTurfer HTTP API: the app's use cases over HTTP, to back up and sync a local-first phone and, later, other clients.

## Getting started

- **Base URL:** pick a server above. Locally, `pnpm --filter @cityturfer/api dev` runs the API on port 8787 and `pnpm run web:dev` serves this page at https://cityturfer.local/swagger with the API under `/api`.
- **Status:** sign-in, backup and restore are live: health, auth, `/v1/me`, consents, activity upload/read/rename/delete, track, gap routes, the changes feed, the Home City, the data export (e-mailed link) and account deletion. Server turf is planned. The rest is designed but **planned**: its summary starts with `[planned]`, it carries `x-cityturfer-status: planned` and answers `501` once auth and validation pass. Live data routes answer `503 storage.unavailable` when the server has no database.
- **Auth:** `POST /v1/auth/codes` with an e-mail, then `POST /v1/auth/sign-in` with the 6-digit code from the e-mail: the answer's `token` goes in `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (button **Authorize**) for about 60 days (sliding); `DELETE /v1/auth/session` signs out. Device tokens (`API_TOKENS`) keep working for one more release. A missing token answers `401` *before* the input is validated. Locally the dev server prints the code (and with `AUTH_FIXED_CODE=000000`, addresses `@e2e.cityturfer.test` sign in with `000000`); `dev-token` works for user `admin` on PGlite.
- **Consent:** activity and Home City writes need `PUT /v1/me/consents/cloud-sync` with `granted: true` first (else `403 consent.required`); Apple Health activities also `apple-health-in-cloud-sync`.
- **Headers you send:** `Content-Type: application/json`; `Content-Encoding: gzip` for long tracks; `If-Match` to change an existing activity; `CityTurfer-Client: ios/0.8.0+123` (old clients may get `426 client.too-old`).
- **Headers you get:** `X-Request-Id` on every answer (quote it when reporting a problem), `ETag` on activities, `Location` on 201/202, `Retry-After` and `RateLimit` on 429.
- **Limits:** request and response bodies ≤ 4.5 MB (Vercel); ≤ 40,000 points per track; gzip bodies inflate to ≤ 16 MB.

## Sync flow (phone ↔ server)

The phone is local-first and authoritative for what it recorded; the server stores activities with their tracks and recomputes everything derived (summaries, turf). Writes are keyed by ids the phone mints, so every request can be retried.

**First upload of an existing history**
1. `PUT /v1/me/consents/cloud-sync` (and `apple-health-in-cloud-sync` to include Apple Health imports).
2. `GET /v1/sync/changes` without a cursor, every page: what the server already has (the manifest).
3. For each local activity, oldest first (never `demo-…`): absent → `PUT /v1/activities/{id}`; same `trackHash` → done; different → `PUT` with `If-Match`; tombstoned → delete it locally.
4. `PUT /v1/activities/{id}/gap-routes` once the phone checked the gaps (an empty list when there are none); `PUT /v1/turf/home-city`.
5. Keep the last `nextCursor`.

**Restore to a new phone**
1. Sign in; `GET /v1/sync/changes` without a cursor while `hasMore` (entries carry ids, names, versions and `trackHash`, no geometry; a page ends at `limit` or about 1 MB).
2. Per activity: `GET /v1/activities/{id}` (summary, gap routes, `gapsCheckedAt`) and `GET /v1/activities/{id}/track`. Store them as restored: never upload them back.
3. Apply tombstones and the Home City; keep the last `nextCursor`.

**Every day after**
- **Push** from the outbox: recorded → `PUT`; track corrected → `PUT` + `If-Match`; renamed → `PATCH`; deleted → `DELETE`; gaps estimated → `PUT …/gap-routes`; Home City → `PUT /v1/turf/home-city`.
- **Pull** on launch and foreground: `GET /v1/sync/changes?cursor=…` while `hasMore`; fetch `GET /v1/activities/{id}/track` (with `If-None-Match`) only when `trackHash` is new; apply tombstones by deleting locally. Pull **before** importing from Apple Health, so a workout recorded on another phone is not imported twice.

**Conflicts:** same content → `200` (replay). Stale `If-Match` → `412`: pull, re-apply, retry. Different content without `If-Match` → `428`. Deleted id → `410 activity.deleted`: delete wins. Renames and the Home City: last write wins. Invalid cursor → `410 sync.cursor-expired`: start again without one.

## Errors

Every error is `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457) with a stable `code`. `detail` is for people and never repeats input values; a `400` lists JSON pointers in `errors[]`.

| code | status | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid-request` | 400 | Invalid request |
| `auth.missing` | 401 | Missing bearer token |
| `auth.invalid` | 401 | Invalid or expired token |
| `auth.invalid-code` | 401 | Wrong or expired code: ask for a new one |
| `consent.required` | 403 | Give the cloud-sync consent first |
| `not-found` | 404 | Not found |
| `activity.deleted` | 410 | Activity was deleted |
| `sync.cursor-expired` | 410 | Sync cursor expired: sync again without a cursor |
| `export.gone` | 410 | This download link was used or has expired |
| `precondition-failed` | 412 | The resource changed since your version |
| `payload-too-large` | 413 | Request body too large |
| `unsupported-media-type` | 415 | Unsupported content type or encoding |
| `activity.track-too-short` | 422 | A track needs at least two points |
| `activity.ends-before-start` | 422 | The activity ends before it starts |
| `activity.invalid-name` | 422 | Names are 1 to 80 characters |
| `activity.track-hash-mismatch` | 422 | trackHash does not match the track |
| `activity.renamed-in-future` | 422 | renamedAt is more than 5 minutes ahead of the server |
| `activity.source-mismatch` | 422 | source does not match the id (hk-… is apple-health) |
| `home-city.unknown` | 422 | Not a catalogue city |
| `export.no-email` | 422 | The account has no e-mail to send the export link to |
| `client.too-old` | 426 | Update the app to sync |
| `precondition-required` | 428 | Send If-Match to change an existing resource |
| `rate-limited` | 429 | Too many requests |
| `auth.rate-limited` | 429 | Too many codes or sign-ins: wait and try again |
| `internal` | 500 | Something went wrong |
| `not-implemented` | 501 | Not implemented yet |
| `storage.unavailable` | 503 | Storage is not available: retry later |

## Units and formats

JSON in camelCase. SI units with a suffix (`distanceM`, `movingS`, `areaKm2`). Timestamps ISO 8601 UTC; an activity may carry its IANA `timeZone` for display — the server derives nothing from local time. Coordinates `[lon, lat]` (GeoJSON order); bounding boxes `[west, south, east, north]`. Track points `[lon, lat, t, segment, altitudeM]`. `trackHash` = SHA-256 hex of `JSON.stringify(track.points)` (no whitespace, ECMAScript number formatting, upload order); the server computes it, so sending it is optional. Turf cells are H3 indexes (resolution 11).

## Privacy

GPS tracks, turf cells and the Home City are personal data. Cloud sync needs the `cloud-sync` consent; everything can be exported (`POST /v1/me/exports`) and erased (`DELETE /v1/me`). Nothing of it is logged: logs hold the route pattern, status, duration, request id and user id. Examples on this page use public landmarks (Warsaw Old Town).

bearerAuth.description: A session token from `POST /v1/auth/sign-in` (e-mailed code, about 60 days, sliding), or — for one more release — a device token minted with `pnpm --filter @cityturfer/api run token:new -- <userId>` (the server knows only its SHA-256, env `API_TOKENS`).

Location.description: Where the created resource or job lives.

RateLimit.description: Remaining quota of the current window (IETF RateLimit header).

coreVersion.description: Version of `@cityturfer/core` the server computes summaries with.

database.description: Whether the database answers a trivial query (no details). Live data routes answer 503 unless `ok`.

CodeRequested.description: Empty: the same answer whether or not the e-mail has an account.

detail.description: For people; never holds input values or coordinates.

errors.description: Only on 400 `invalid-request`: which fields are invalid (the first 20).

code.description: Why it is invalid (zod issue code).

token.description: Bearer token: send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Store it in the keychain; never log it.

code.description: The 6-digit code from the e-mail (works once, 10 minutes).

displayName.description: Falls back to the user id.

createdAt.description: When the server first saw the account.

status.description: `pending`: being built; `ready`: the link was e-mailed; `downloaded`: fetched at least once (still works until `expiresAt`); `expired`: 24 h passed, or a consent was withdrawn; `failed`: nothing was sent, ask again at once.

expiresAt.description: The e-mailed link works until then (24 h).

DataExportJob.description: An export of everything the server holds for the account: a zip with `data.json` (account, consents, activities with tracks and gap routes, tombstones, Home City) and one GPX 1.1 file per activity. The download link is only in the e-mail and works until `expiresAt`.

policyVersion.description: Privacy policy version shown to the user.

ConsentPurpose.description: `cloud-sync`: back up and sync activities with their GPS tracks. `apple-health-in-cloud-sync`: include workouts imported from Apple Health (decision D2). Without `cloud-sync` the server accepts no uploads.

nextCursor.description: Always present: store it and pass it next time, even when `hasMore` is false.

hasMore.description: True: ask again now with `nextCursor`. A page ends at `limit` changes or about 1 MB.

changedAt.description: When the server recorded the change.

ActivityUpserted.description: Created or changed (track, name, gap routes). Download the track only when `activity.trackHash` differs from yours.

version.description: Grows by one with every change; the `ETag` is `"v<version>"`.

trackHash.description: Canonical track hash: SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the UTF-8 bytes of `JSON.stringify(track.points)` — no whitespace, points `[lon, lat, t, segment, altitudeM | null]` in upload order, numbers in ECMAScript shortest round-trip form (what `JSON.stringify` writes). The server computes it; a hash the client sends must match (422 `activity.track-hash-mismatch`). Tells other devices whether to download the track again.

ActivityFeedEntry.description: An activity in the changes feed: no preview or numbers (pages stay small). Fetch `GET /v1/activities/{id}` and, when `trackHash` is new, `GET /v1/activities/{id}/track`.

ActivitySource.description: `recording`: a finished Recording Session; `apple-health`: imported from Apple Health (`hk-…` id, needs the `apple-health-in-cloud-sync` consent); `import`: any other import. Demo history (`demo-…`) is never uploaded.

changedAt.description: When the server recorded the change.

ActivityTombstone.description: Deleted: delete it locally and never upload it again (it would answer 410).

changedAt.description: When the server recorded the change.

The server computes it; a hash the client sends must match (422 `activity.track-hash-mismatch`). Tells other devices whether to download the track again.

Track.description: Every point of an activity, in time order. Personal data.

TrackPoint.description: Columns: `[lon, lat, t, segment, altitudeM]` — longitude and latitude (degrees, WGS 84), time (epoch ms, UTC), segment number (a new segment starts after a pause or GPS gap; segments are never bridged), altitude in metres or null. Accuracy and speed are not sent (data minimisation, decision D1).

resumedSegments.description: Segments that began with a manual Resume; null when unknown.

renamedAt.description: When a `PATCH` last renamed it (the phone’s time); null when never renamed.

gapsCheckedAt.description: When the phone last checked the GPS gaps (`PUT …/gap-routes`, an empty list included); null when never checked or since the track changed. A restoring phone that sees a time here does not estimate the gaps again.

movingS.description: Moving time of this kilometre (not cumulative).

GapRoute.description: A street route the phone estimated across a GPS gap: counted in distance, drawn dashed, never claimed as turf. The server never computes these (D3).

name.description: The new name (1–80 characters once trimmed).

renamedAt.description: When the user renamed it on the phone: the latest `renamedAt` wins (offline-safe).

checkedAt.description: When the phone checked the gaps (`gapsCheckedAt`).

GapRoutesUpload.description: Replaces every gap route of the activity; an empty list means checked, no gaps.

id.description: H3 cell index (res 11, or coarser when aggregated).

TurfCell.description: No polygon: clients draw the boundary from the H3 id (h3-js `cellToBoundary`).

Claim.description: The cells one activity covered. A cell is *new* for the claim with the earliest `(startedAt, activityId)` that covers it (decision D4), so the answer does not depend on upload order; it can change when an older activity arrives later.

cityId.description: A catalogue city id, or null to clear.

chosenAt.description: When the user chose it on the phone; the latest `chosenAt` wins (offline-safe).

Withdrawing a consent deletes the zip and expires the link.

Without `cloud-sync` granted, activity and Home City writes answer `403 consent.required`. **Withdrawing deletes the server copy only** (never anything on a phone), at once and without new tombstones or feed entries: `cloud-sync` → every activity with its track and gap routes and the Home City (the account, consents and existing tombstones stay — ids and times only, no location data — so turning backup on again re-uploads everything but what was deleted, which still answers `410`); `apple-health-in-cloud-sync` → every Apple Health (`hk-…`) activity. get.description:
Upserts, tombstones and Home City choices in server order since `cursor` (use case ListChanges). Without a cursor it lists everything the server holds for the user — the manifest a phone compares with its own history on the first upload. Each activity, tombstone and the Home City appears once, at its latest change. Activity entries carry no geometry: a page ends at `limit` changes or about 1 MB, whichever comes first.

Pull on launch, on foreground and after pushing; repeat while `hasMore`. Changes made by the calling device come back too: apply them idempotently (same `version` → nothing to do).

**Restore to a new phone:** page from no cursor (the manifest), then for each activity `GET /v1/activities/{id}` and `GET /v1/activities/{id}/track`; apply tombstones and the Home City.

put.summary: Upload or replace a finished activity
put.description:
Stores the activity with its track under the id the phone minted (use cases ImportActivity and, for a corrected track, CorrectTrack). The server recomputes distance, time and splits from the track with the shared core and computes the canonical `trackHash` (a hash the client sends must match). Needs the `cloud-sync` consent (Apple Health activities also `apple-health-in-cloud-sync`).

- **New id** → `201` with `ETag` and `Location`.
- **Same content again** (same track, name and fields) → `200`, unchanged: replays are safe.
- **Different content** → send `If-Match` with the current `ETag`: `200` and version + 1; a stale one → `412`, none → `428` (both carry the current `ETag`). A new track drops the stored gap routes: send them again.
- **Deleted id** → `410 activity.deleted`: delete the activity locally too.

`source` must match the id: `hk-…` ids are `apple-health` and only they may be (else `422 activity.source-mismatch`).

Bodies are limited to 4.5 MB: send long tracks with `Content-Encoding: gzip`.

patch.description: Use case RenameActivity. The last write wins on `renamedAt` (decision D6): an equal or older rename answers `200` with the activity unchanged. A `renamedAt` more than 5 minutes ahead of the server is `422 activity.renamed-in-future`. A new name bumps the version and appears in the changes feed. (A `PUT` that replaces the activity with another name sets it but keeps `renamedAt`: rename with `PATCH`.) `If-Match` is optional; a stale one answers `412`. Needs the `cloud-sync` consent.

delete.description: Deletes the activity, its track and gap routes, releases its turf (use case DeleteActivity) and leaves a tombstone (the id and when; no personal data): other devices learn it from `GET /v1/sync/changes`, and a later upload of the same id answers `410`. Idempotent: `204` even when already gone or never uploaded. No undelete (D5). Works without the `cloud-sync` consent: it only removes data.

put.description: Replaces the street routes the phone estimated across GPS gaps (use case SaveGapRoutes; decision D3) and records that the gaps were checked (`gapsCheckedAt` in the detail). Send an **empty** `routes` list when the phone checked and found no gaps. Display only: they add to distance and moving time and are drawn dashed, never claimed as turf. Idempotent; version + 1 when they changed or the activity had not been checked yet. Needs the `cloud-sync` consent.
